intro_paras: One family per block: what the code does, read from the code, and what changed between revisions. Written by an LLM session, each sentence tied to the one revision it was read from - a family whose file has changed since is marked stale. This is a description, not a measurement, and it decides nothing.

Families and labels. A family is two or more strategies whose names share a stem and whose code is similar (similar stems such as BB_RPB_TSL and BB_RPB_TSL_RNG are merged); a strategy without a sibling is not a family. Labels are read from the entry and exit code by Haiku 4.5, each with a verbatim code snippet as evidence (evidence/STRATEGY_LABELS.json). A family carries a label when more than half of its members do; other labels show as variants. Labels describe the logic, not its quality, and a family without a written description shows its members only. Where the description was written by DeepSeek Flash from the fact sheet (the same request that gives the second opinion on the label), it says so in evidence/STRATEGY_LABELS.json and is a reading of the code, not a test result.

families.name: Nostalgia
families.idea_html:
The X line is a trading system rather than a signal: an entry built from a long list of indexed conditions, a custom_exit of several hundred lines, adjust_trade_position for DCA and a set of _bad_trade_controller_* handlers that decide when a losing trade gets de-risked, held or closed. The revisions grow by adding whole blocks - the informative 1d/4h/1h/15m indicator sets, the derisk handlers, the volume-normalised helpers - while the entry stays a basket of conditions that can be switched on and off per index.

Caveat: This is the only family on this page that the bundle cannot describe: the indicator list is capped at 40 entries and the method list is longer than one screen, so no count on this page says how large the strategy really is. Read the strategy in the corpus, not the summary.
version_rows: 13,585 lines, the smallest release. The X2_* strategies grow from 742 to 1,393 lines, add __init__/_load/_remove_profit_target and pull the 5m and 1h indicator blocks apart into named methods - the structural change of the line.

40,162 to 66,190 lines. The growth sits in the informative indicator sets (155-207 lines each in X8) and in the exit machinery; X6 adds the mode handlers _handle_derisk_mode, _handle_scalp_mode and _handle_top_coins_mode, which is the first time the strategy switches behaviour per regime instead of per condition.

39,071 lines and the revision the description is read from - smaller than X7 again, which fits the picture of a line that is rewritten rather than only appended to. It carries the volume-normalised helpers (OBV change, Chaikin money flow, fast percentage change) and a custom_exit of 557 lines.
position_adjustment_enable, minimal_roi and startup_candle_count (800 against 480) alternate between adjacent strategies, so they are variants of the releases above, not further releases.

other_descriptions.idea_html:
The same basket-of-conditions entry as the X line, but with the exit assembled from a library of named sell functions - sell_over_main (174 lines), sell_under_main (163), sell_pump_main (374), sell_ichi, sell_long_mode, sell_quick_mode, sell_duration_main - between which custom_sell (201 lines) selects. That is where the revision differences sit: populate_buy_trend is 634 lines in the revision read here, whereas the exit side is a set of replaceable parts.

Caveat: The canonical file of the revision read here is a repaired file (repair/patched/repos/Foxel05_freqtrade-stuff/...), so the sentence describes the repaired revision. The same family is also present from upstream repositories, and the repaired file is the one the corpus measures.

The ancestor of the Next and X lines, and where their shape comes from: the entry is a long list of numbered buy conditions that each consult the 1h informative averages, and the exit is a set of named sell routines rather than one rule. It does not change its mind over sixteen revisions - it accretes: 150 lines at V1, 2,001 at V7, 4,855 in the last revision the corpus holds, all with the same structure.

Caveat: Fewer than half of the sixteen strategies here are distinct designs. The same three settings (stoploss -0.99 against -0.277, process_only_new_candles, startup_candle_count 400 against 480) alternate between adjacent numbered strategies, so the corpus holds variants of a revision rather than sixteen releases one after another.

families.name: E0V1E
families.idea_html:
A 5m scalper whose entry is a bundle of conditions ORed together rather than one rule: EMA(8/16) against EMA/SMA(15) and RSI(4/14/20), the stochastic-fast fastk, and a Bollinger band around the typical price are collected into a list and reduced with `lambda x, y: x | y`, so any single member can open a trade. The exit side is where the work sits: a custom_stoploss that locks in above 1% profit and treats trades tagged 'ewo' differently, plus a custom_exit that reads the fastk and RSI columns of the current candle. minimal_roi and the 0.99 stoploss are nominal next to that.

Caveat: The custom_stoploss branches on the entry tag (`if 'ewo' in enter_tags`), so the same file holds two different exit rules depending on which condition opened the trade - a reader who evaluates only the stoploss number will read the risk wrong.
version_rows: The only chronology this family has, and it comes from the dates in five file names: the ROI goes {'0': 10} -> {'0': 0.02, '120': 0.01} -> {'0': 10} -> {'0': 1} -> {'0': 10}, the stoploss -0.13 -> -0.18 -> -0.27 -> back to -0.99, startup_candle_count 121 -> 120 -> 20, and the 2024-01-11 revision adds ta.CCI(20) and switches DCA (position_adjustment_enable) off again. Five dated strategies, four steps, and they are steps of a scalar search rather than four designs.

Their numbers are the harvest's collision counter, not versions, and the content proves it: adjacent strategies reverse each other - E0V1E_22 to _23 steps stoploss -0.18 -> -0.99 and startup_candle_count 120 -> 20, and _23 to _24 steps both back again. What the corpus holds is a parameter fan written out in file order, so this page lists the strategies and states no order for them.
Across the fan there are two shapes: 74-93 lines with 5-8 indicator calls and no custom hooks, and 121-158 lines with 11 indicator calls plus custom_stoploss and custom_exit. Every strategy runs 5m.

families.name: BB_RPB
families.idea_html:
A Bollinger strategy with a pull-back condition ('RPB', Real Pull Back) and a Bollinger middle-band exit, wrapped around a state machine for the buy itself: `trailing_buy`, `trailing_buy_info`, `trailing_buy_offset` and `current_trailing_profit_ratio` chase a falling price before the entry is taken, and `custom_sell` (87-107 lines) decides the exit. The docstring names its source - a blog post and a GitHub project - so the family's lineage is documented in the file.

Caveat: The canonical file of the strategy read here, and of the v104 strategy, are repaired files under repair/patched/ rather than repository files; the sentence describes the repaired revision, which is the one the corpus measures.
version_rows: 349 to 753 lines and 25 to 40 indicator calls (the cap applies to v104, so 40 is a floor). Both are the same design: normal_tf_indicators and informative_1h_indicators split the work, and v104 doubles the informative block from 50 to ... lines while custom_sell grows from 87 to 107.

families.name: Ichimoku
families.idea_html:
The Ichimoku cloud used as a filter around a Tenkan/Kijun cross rather than as the signal itself: the long needs the Tenkan line to cross above the Kijun line while the cloud is red, and the short is not the mirror but a different rule. Later revisions keep the same cross and read the cloud from a higher timeframe through informative_pairs, or replace the candle with its Heikin-Ashi version and compare that against the daily Senkou A/B - so the family is one idea read against different chart types.

Caveat: The entry in the strategy read here buys a Tenkan/Kijun cross while `cloud_red` is true, i.e. while the cloud is bearish - the opposite of the textbook reading, where a cross is only taken in the direction of the cloud. Its `populate_sell_trend` also assigns an empty tuple, so exits in this revision come from minimal_roi alone.
version_rows: 4h, 42-60 lines, two to four indicator calls, and one line of buy logic that changes from revision to revision: crossed_above(tenkan, kijun), then crossed_below, then the same cross against senkou_b, then against close. The ROI value alternates between {'0': 10} and {'0': 100} while nothing else moves.

The chart moves out to 1d (v17) and back to 4h (v18), and informative_pairs grows to five lines: the daily Tenkan is pulled into the 4h frame, which is the first revision that reads two timeframes at once.

Three strategies that add the same three settings (process_only_new_candles, startup_candle_count 150, use_sell_signal) and lose them again in the next one, so they are variants of one shape rather than a progression. v37 is the Heikin-Ashi variant (file Ichimoku_v37_HeikinAshi.py): ha_close of the 4h against senkou_a_1d/senkou_b_1d plus cloud_green_1d.
188 lines at 5m, the only intraday member of the cloud family, and the only strategy that sets ticker_interval and timeframe at once - a file written for two freqtrade API generations.

Where the Elliot and Ichimoku lines meet: the Elliot frame (Hull moving average(50), EMA, RSI 4/14/20) with the Ichimoku conditions added to the entry, and a protections() block of 35 lines that none of the other Elliot strategies carry. All ten strategies are the same size and shape - 176 to 204 lines, 8 to 10 indicator calls, 4 conditions - so this family is a set of states of one file rather than a development.

families.name: Cluc
families.idea_html:
The 'Cluc' band entry taken over from the CombinedBinHAndCluc family, but computed on Heikin-Ashi candles and filtered by a 1h ROCR: the buy needs rocr_1h above a threshold and the band event (lower band above zero, a band distance and a body above their thresholds, a lower wick smaller than a fraction of the distance) on the Heikin-Ashi close, and the sell uses a Fisher transform. The stop is a custom_stoploss that compares the current profit against two profit targets.

Caveat: This stem is the base of three families on this page - ClucHAnix, ClucHAnixV* and ClucHAnix_5m - and the CombinedBinHAndCluc line uses the same band event without the Heikin-Ashi wrapper. They are not code-identical, so no duplicate verdict covers them, but they share one entry rule.
version_rows: V1 is 278 lines with 24 indicator calls; V2 is 200 lines with 12 - and gains DCA and a 1d BTC informative block (MACD on informative_btc_1d) with custom_stake_amount and adjust_trade_position. The file gets smaller while the strategy gets more machinery.

154 to 277 lines. position_adjustment_enable switches on at ClucHAnix_2, off at ClucHAnix2_562 and on again at ClucHAnix_3, and the ROI flips between {'0': 100} and {'70': 0} three times in the same range - the clearest variant list in this batch.
The one strategy that changes the indicator frame: 204 lines with 13 calls, ta.EMA(dataframe, 14) and ta.RSI instead of the Heikin-Ashi EMA(3/50) and ROCR pair.

families.name: Zaratustra
families.idea_html:
One comparison decides everything: while RSI(7) sits above RSI(14) the strategy is long, while it sits below it is short, and each side is closed as soon as the two cross back. There is no other filter and no signal-per-candle logic - the position is a state of the RSI spread. Exits in practice come from the risk settings, which are deliberately tight: 1% stoploss, 0.1% trailing stop and a flat 1% take-profit.

Caveat: The site's own family table advertises this family as 10x with a trailing stop. This revision's leverage() returns 1, so the published description and the code in the corpus disagree about position size - the description there may belong to a different revision or to a bot configuration.
version_rows: The early design steps: V3 runs 15m with one indicator call and no exit condition at all, V4 moves to 5m and brings the Bollinger/crossed_above condition, the ROI ladder and a 1.3% trailing stop.

This stretch reads like a hyperopt walk rather than a design history: the ROI ladder is removed at V5 and returns at V6, DCA is switched on at V8 and off at V9, max_open_trades alternates between -1 and 10, the indicator count climbs to 17 (V19) and falls back to 4 (V25), and the stoploss moves between -0.125 and -0.99 without a direction.
The end of the line leaves the 5m chart: V27 runs 15m, V28/V29/V31 run 1h, and V31 is down to two indicator calls (RSI 7 and RSI 14) with the RSI spread as the only rule.

A separate branch that keeps the DCA idea: 183-204 lines with adjust_trade_position (53-71 lines) in ZaratustraDCA2_06/_07/_063, and ZaratustraDCA5 at 572 lines with 17 indicator calls and 23 conditions, the largest member of the family.

families.name: BBRSI
families.idea_html:
Two lines of code carry the idea: buy when the RSI is above 25 while the close is below the lower Bollinger band at one standard deviation, sell when the RSI is above 95 while the close is above the one-sigma upper band. The RSI threshold works as a filter in the opposite direction to the usual reading - it rules out the deepest falls - and the two bands are plotted at one and four standard deviations, so the entry and the exit use different widths.

Caveat: This stem, BBRSI and BbandRsi are the same idea under three spellings and three cases, which is why the ranking counts them as three of the largest families. The RSI level also changes between strategies (25 here, 33 in BBRSI3366), so the threshold is part of the tuning, not of the design.
version_rows: The fourteen strategies sit at 30m (bbrsi_v2, bbrsi_v3), 15m (_2, _941), 5m (_116, _410), 1h (five strategies) and 4h (the undecorated one). The signal is the same in all of them and only the ROI and stoploss move, so the family is one strategy swept over timeframes.

The outlier: 117 lines at 5m with 13 conditions instead of 2, an informative frame and a stoploss of -0.327 with a ROI of {'0': 0.064, '28': 0.048, '56': 0} - a hyperopt result rather than a hand-written revision.
Several strategies carry hyperopt output in their settings verbatim (stoploss -0.4275704128061333, ROI {'0': 0.07916501011003861, ...}), which is where the long decimals on this page come from.

other_descriptions.idea_html:
The same Mynt port as BbandRsi but with the exit turned around: buy when the close is below the lower Bollinger band (with no RSI condition on the entry at all), sell when the RSI is above 90 and the close is above the *middle* band - so the exit is a momentum confirmation rather than a band touch, and the band width is 4 standard deviations instead of 2. The docstring still says 'Default Strategy provided by freqtrade bot', because the port was made from the framework's example.

Caveat: The ROI and stoploss in most strategies are raw hyperopt output (stoploss -0.3639404146663022, ROI {'0': 0.18958106762410365, ...}), and BBRSIv2 is the odd strategy with nine conditions and an informative frame. This family is the second of three spellings of one idea; see BBRSI, bbrsi and BbandRsi.

families.name: Solipsis
families.idea_html:
Momentum read from the RMI (RSI applied to a ROC) plus a rolling count of up-candles, with the exit split in two: a custom stoploss that can decay, trail or work dynamically, and a `min_roi_reached_dynamic` that replaces the ROI table with a function of trade duration. It is a scalp at 5m whose exits are its real content - the entry conditions are short in every revision.

Caveat: Those with a number in their name (Solipsis3 to Solipsis6) repeat the `_v` revisions with one parameter moved each: Solipsis5 to Solipsis6 produces the same seventeen changes as Solipsis_v2_5 to Solipsis_v2_6. So the stem holds one design in many states, and the numbering is a harvest counter rather than a history.
version_rows: 567 to 474 lines, and the custom stoploss goes from 28 lines to 20 and is switched off - the first of several times this strategy changes its exit philosophy.

378 to 428 lines; v2_6 writes the stoploss as custustom_stop['decay-start'] instead of a number, i.e. the stop is computed from a parameter dictionary, and the informative pairs grow to Bollinger bands on higher timeframes.

The single largest step in the family (125 changes): startup_candle_count doubles from 72 to 233, the ROI ladder is replaced by a flat {'0': 0.01}, and v4 carries 33 indicator calls. v4, v4_2 and v4_3 are all 375 lines with the same shape.
275 lines and 12 indicator calls - the smallest revision, and the one that abandons custom_stoploss for a 59-line custom_sell while keeping the dynamic ROI.

families.name: EI3v2_tag_cofi_green
families.idea_html:
An 'EI3 v2' confluence entry - Hull moving average(50), SMA(9), RSI(4/8/14/20) - combined with a pump-and-dump veto: a volume ratio above 5 (short mean against long mean) sets a `dont_buy` column that blocks entries, while a BTC informative block and a protections() block shape the rest. `adjust_trade_position` (38 lines) adds to a position, so the strategy can average into a losing trade.

Caveat: This family is the clearest case on the page of a name carrying no order: eleven of its twelve strategies extract to the same fifteen indicator calls and the same thirteen conditions, and the differences between them are one parameter or one line. The version numbers in the ids order the corpus's arrival, not the author's work.
version_rows: 331 lines, 15 indicator calls, 13 conditions. Their differences are visible in one place each: _2_3 and _2_4 move a line inside adjust_trade_position, _5 replaces the ROI {'0': 0.99} with a ladder, _7 grows adjust_trade_position from 37 to 41 lines.
The pair differs in exactly one setting: startup_candle_count 400 against 1999, which is the number a hyperopt run found rather than a decision. Two corpus strategies for one change.

families.idea_html: NotAnotherSMAOffSetStrategy_V2: This 5m strategy computes EMAs, HMA50, EMA100, SMA9, EWO, RSI fast/slow, and volume oscillators. Entries require price below a chosen buy EMA offset, low RSI fast/RSI, EWO above a threshold, and volume oscillator in certain bands, with several variants tagged ewo1/ewo3. Exits trigger when price is above a sell EMA offset with rising RSI fast versus RSI slow, or an alternative HMA50 condition; trailing stop is enabled and stoploss is -0.35.

families.name: BinH
families.idea_html: Two designs share this stem, and the page keeps them together because the name does. BinHV27 is the multi-filter one - RSI(5), an EMA of an RSI frame, ADX with its +DI/-DI and the EMAs of both, plus EMA/SMA 60/120/240 - where the long needs the close below both slow averages, -DI above its own EMA and RSI not falling, and the sell side has its own reversal machine ('preparechangetrendconfirm', 'bigdown'). BinHV45 is a 1-minute Bollinger scalp at a window of 40 that uses the same bbdelta/closedelta/tail entry as the CombinedBinHAndCluc family, so the two branches are related by the entry construction rather than by lineage.
version_rows: 124 lines, 22 indicator calls, no custom stop, minimal_roi {'0': 1} and stoploss -0.5. Its variants move in one step each: _1, _3 and _254 add custom_stoploss, use_sell_signal and startup_candle_count 240; _2 runs 15m; _32 writes the timeframe as '5T'; _747 adds two more indicator calls; _253 and _387 come back to the bare shape.

1m, 45-85 lines, one or two indicator calls (Bollinger at window=40); the strategies differ only in minimal_roi (0.0125 against 0.20233), stoploss (-0.05 against -0.13348) and whether a trailing stop is armed. _2 is the outlier at 15m with a ROI of 0.99.

Both branches number their strategies with harvest counters; adjacent strategies reverse each other (V27_253 to _254 switches minimal_roi 1 <-> 100, custom stop off/on and startup count none/240, and _254 to _387 switches them back), so nothing here is claimed to be a history.

families.name: roger
families.idea_html:
The numbered strategies are one line of work: each iteration adds a candlestick-pattern filter to a VWAP/EMA/RSI/ATR frame, until roger27 trades `bullish_conditions | candlestick_patterns & macd_condition` and stops the trade on peak-profit drawdown. The undecorated strategy is a different design under the same stem - a VWAP band system with RSI(16) percentile bands and no candle patterns at all - so the stem holds two strategies, and this page says so rather than averaging them into one sentence.

Caveat: `roger` (88 lines, nine conditions) and `VWAPStrategy` (73 lines) use the same construction: a per-candle state column asking whether the body touched the daily VWAP from below, above or both, plus RSI percentile bands. They are not code-identical, which is why no duplicate verdict covers them, but a reader should expect them to behave alike.
version_rows: 45 to 101 lines and 2 to 17 indicator calls: the frame (EMA 50/200, Bollinger, RSI) is set up at roger2-roger4, can_short appears at roger4 and toggles, and from roger6 the candle patterns start arriving one per strategy (CDL3BLACKCROWS, CDLENGULFING, CDL3WHITESOLDIERS, CDL3INSIDE, CDL3OUTSIDE, CDLGRAVESTONEDOJI, CDLHAMMER, CDLINVERTEDHAMMER, CDLSHOOTINGSTAR, CDLENGULFING).
The ATR trailing stop arrives (use_custom_stoploss True at roger14), the ATR length moves 14 -> 150 -> 4, and roger21 adds calc_stop_loss_pct and on_trade_close, i.e. the exit becomes stateful.
160 lines, 21 indicator calls, ta.MACD added: the entry is bullish_conditions | candlestick_patterns & macd_condition and the stop reacts to a peak-profit drawdown above 2%, then 10%.
88 lines, no candle patterns: VWAP_signal, RSI(16) with lower_band/upper_band from percentiles, BB(14, 2) and a 14-line ATR stop. Same stem, different strategy.

families.name: GeneTrader_gen
families.idea_html: A generator's output, labelled by the generator itself: every class name carries the generation, a Unix timestamp and a counter, which makes this the one family on the page that can be ordered by time from its names alone. The population alternates between two blueprints - a 112-135-line variant with 8 indicator calls, and a 507-621-line variant with DCA, an informative BTC frame and one to four RSI periods - so the generator was comparing a small and a large body plan, not refining one design.
version_rows: Three strategies (gen3, gen5, gen30), 112 lines each with 8 indicator calls and no DCA - the earliest state in the corpus and the smallest.
gen1, 507 lines with 26 indicator calls and a ROI ladder: the first large member, ten weeks after the small ones.

Seven strategies of 135 lines at 8 indicator calls, written within two days of each other. The generation number does not track the body plan - gen10 appears here and again among the large strategies - so the generator's numbering counts its own rounds, not the strategy size.

Six strategies of 620/621 lines with position_adjustment_enable, ROI {'0': 100}, startup_candle_count 168 and adjust_trade_position (87 lines). The 135-line strategies written in the same window carry ROI {'0': 1} and no DCA, so the two blueprints were run side by side rather than one after the other.

families.name: SMAOffsetProtectOpt
families.idea_html:
A dip buyer on a single moving average: the long opens when the close falls a hyperopt-tuned fraction below an EMA of a tuned length, and closes when the close crosses below a second EMA; a higher timeframe EMA is pulled in through informative pairs, and 'protect' is the file's own name for the parameter block that gates both sides. The exit is nominal - the ROI ladder and a 0.2 to 0.5 stoploss do the work.

Caveat: The V1_* strategies alternate between two states - ROI {'0': 100} with stoploss -0.15, and a ROI ladder with stoploss -0.5 - at least three times across ten strategies, so only the endpoints of the family are designs.

families.name: VWAPStrategy
families.idea_html:
A VWAP band system: for every candle the code asks whether the body touched the daily VWAP from below, from above or both, stores that as a state column, and then asks the RSI(16) to sit below its own 10th percentile (or the mirror, above the 90th) while the close is outside the Bollinger band - so the trade needs a VWAP event, an RSI extreme and a band break at once, joined with reduce(lambda x, y: x & y, conditions). The stop is a custom_stoploss that is rewritten in almost every strategy of the family; the entry is not.

Caveat: These strategies are numbered by the harvest, and the numbers do not order them: VWAPStrategy_11 has stoploss -0.1, _12 has -0.2 and drops the trailing stop, and the undecorated strategy has -0.07 again. The table below lists variants, not a history.
version_rows: Unchanged across all 18 strategies: the VWAP_signal loop, RSI(16) with percentile bands, Bollinger(14, 2). This is one of the few families where the signal and the risk can be separated cleanly.

custom_stoploss is rewritten in nearly every strategy - 35 -> 31 -> 28 -> 27 -> 25 -> 28 -> 18 -> 17 -> 21 lines - and changes its idea twice: it starts from the ATR, then compares the current profit against fixed steps, then works from trade.initial_stop_loss, and VWAPStrategy_1 arms it with ta.atr(length=150) where the undecorated strategy uses length=7.

use_custom_stoploss is absent at _2 and present from _03 on; the stoploss moves between -0.2 and -0.1 twice; trailing_stop, trailing_stop_positive and the offset appear and disappear together (at _12 and again at _18). None of the moves is reversed later in a way that would let one call this a direction.

families.name: ichi
families.idea_html:
SuperTrend, SSL channels and Ichimoku in one file, with the Ichimoku part used as a depth gauge: `buy_trend_above_senkou_level` decides how many cloud levels the trend has to be above (the condition is checked in up to four steps), so one parameter turns a cloud filter into a stack of filters. The modern strategies keep that structure and stack an EMA ladder (3/6/12/18/24/48/72/96) on the Heikin-Ashi close.

Caveat: Two strategies set their stoploss to an expression rather than a number (stoploss -0.217 * custom_leverage), so the effective risk depends on a module-level value the reader has to find; and ichiV2_1 is a fragment of 55 lines that happens to be in the corpus.
version_rows: The archived original is 84 lines with a stoploss of -0.01 and a 5% ROI ladder; ichiV1 is 157 lines with 17 indicator calls, and ichiV1_6 is the same design at 115 lines.

The 1m revisions: 207 and 156 lines with 34 and 20 conditions, stoploss -0.217 * custom_leverage and a startup_candle_count of 130 against 96 - so these are the revisions that scale the risk with leverage.

ichiV2_2 and V2_5 are 165 and 169 lines with 18 calls and agree except for the risk block ({'0': 0.3} against a flat stoploss of -0.06); ichiV3 documents its own history in the docstring ('the previous version was ichiV2_5') and moves the 1m Heikin-Ashi handling so that the original OHLC is left alone.

families.name: Schism
families.idea_html:
An RMI reversal with a time budget: the RMI (RSI of a ROC) supplies the entry trigger, RSI columns on other timeframes gate it, and the exit is a ROI table that is replaced by `min_roi_reached_entry` and `min_roi_reached_dynamic` - a return that depends on how long the trade has been open and on a growth function. `populate_trades` (56 lines) keeps per-pair state and `check_buy_timeout`/`confirm_trade_entry` decide whether a signal is still valid when the next candle arrives.

Caveat: The corpus holds this family twice under two naming styles. Schism4, Schism5 and Schism6 have the same size, indicator count and condition count as Schism_v1_4, _v1_5 and _v1_6, and consecutive deltas produce the same change lists (41 changes for Schism4 -> Schism5 and for _v1_4 -> _v1_5). They are not code-identical, so no verdict covers them, but treating the six strategies as six revisions would double the family.
version_rows: 225 to 460 lines and 13 to 17 conditions; the growth is the state handling (populate_trades, min_roi_reached_*) rather than the signal. v1_5 is the outlier at 239 lines with 8 indicator calls and only 6 conditions.

families.name: AdxSmas
families.idea_html: A port of a C# bot, and its docstring says so: 'author@: Gert Wohlgemuth converted from: https://github.com/sthewissen/Mynt/blob/master/src/Mynt.Core/Strategies/AdxSmas.cs'. The rule is a two-line crossover - ADX below 25 while SMA(3) crosses above SMA(6) for the long, the mirror for the short - so the trend filter is inverted: trades are only taken when the trend strength is *low*. Both sides can be open, which is what the can_short flag in the settings is for.
version_rows: 49 to 78 lines: v3 adds a 28-line protections() block (stoploss guards, cooldown, max drawdown) and nothing else - the entry and exit methods are unchanged.

The risk block moves: stoploss -0.25 -> -0.15 -> -0.25, the custom_stoploss threshold 0.03 -> 0.04, and custom_stoploss and protections swap lengths (9/28 -> 14/14 -> 9/28) between v5, v6 and v7. The ROI gains a ladder at v7 ({'2160': 0.025, '1440': 0.05, '720': 0.075, '0': 0.1}).

38 lines with five indicator calls: the version without protections and without a custom stoploss, keeping only the crossover and a 0.25 stoploss. It is the skeleton the rest of the family is built on.

families.name: BBMod
families.idea_html:
A Bollinger strategy on the Heikin-Ashi typical price with a VWAP-of-a-higher-timeframe twist: `rolling_vwap` of one frame feeds exponential averages of intermediate columns, those feed further EMAs, and a 1h informative block adds its own set. The entry is a reduced OR of many conditions, the exit a 29-line custom_stoploss over two profit factors, and several strategies add `generate_roi_table` plus DCA - so the family is a modulation of one indicator cascade.

Caveat: Every strategy of this family reaches the 40-entry cap in the indicator list, so none of the counts on this page describes how many indicators these files use. The corpus also holds `BBMod` and `BBMod_7` as one code-identical pair, which is why 13 strategies group into 12 codes.
version_rows: 379 to 818 lines. BBMod1 is more than twice the size of BBMod_1 (370) and the difference is the position_adjustment/DCA block plus the longer condition list (8 against 11 conditions).
835 down to 818 lines: BBMod1_2 drops adjust_trade_position and shortens custom_sell from 62 to 51 lines, and BBMod1_3 differs from BBMod1_2 in code but not in any extracted fact.

316 to 787 lines. position_adjustment_enable switches on at BBMod_5 and off again at BBMod_6, and the Bollinger input alternates between the typical price and the Heikin-Ashi typical price - the same variant pattern as elsewhere in this batch.

461 lines each and code-identical: custom_stoploss 29 lines, populate_indicators 118, populate_indicators_1h 20. The corpus's own duplicate check groups them, and this page lists both because the corpus does.

families.name: GRIDDMIPRICEStrategyFuture
families.idea_html:
A grid, not a signal: the entry compares the close against an EMA threshold while +DI/-DI of an informative timeframe sit above an ADX level, both directions can be taken (can_short True), there is no exit signal at all (`exit_long = ()`), and the position is managed by a 97-line `adjust_trade_position` plus leverage(). The price levels the grid works on are set by custom_stake_amount in v7's 27-line version, so the file is a position manager that happens to have an entry condition.

Caveat: GRIDDMIPRICEStrategyFutureV7 is a degenerate strategy: its informatives and the DI/EMA calls are gone and `enter_long = dataframe['close'] > 0` enters whenever a candle closes - it looks like a hyperopt skeleton. The same corpus also holds it as a code-identical copy under the name ADX_PRICE_GRID_Strategy_Future_v7, one of the duplicate groups the corpus's own check reports.
version_rows: 174 to 192 lines, and the timeframe drops from 4h to 1m with the stoploss going from -0.45 to -2 and the ROI from {'0': 1} to {'0': 100} - a grid strategy that stops pretending to be a swing strategy.
298 to 309 lines: adjust_trade_position grows from 82 to 160 lines and then stabilises at 152, order_filled from 42 to 64, and custom_stake_amount from 6 to 28 - the grid logic is written out here.
270 lines with no indicator call left and enter_long = close > 0: the informative DI/EMA comparisons that V6 still had were removed, which is why this strategy appears to trade on every candle.
187 lines at 5m with the DI/EMA entry back in place and a 5-line custom_stake_amount offset of 0.1 - the shortest version of the design and the one without the v7 machinery.

families.name: Heracles

families.name: ReinforcedSmoothScalp
families.idea_html: A high-frequency scalp, and the only family on this page whose file states its own trading assumption: 'generating a lot of potential buys and make tiny profits on each trade - we recommend to have at least 60 parallel trades at any time to cover non avoidable losses'. The entry wants the open below EMA(5) of the low with ADX above 30, MFI below 30 and a stochastic cross out of oversold, the exit wants the open back at EMA(5) of the high or the stochastic above 70 with CCI above 150, and the ROI is 2% with a 10% stop - a rule set that only works as a population of trades, as the docstring says.

15m with 25-line populate_entry_trend and populate_exit_trend (against 22 and 18 at 1m), which is the same design with the conditions written out one per line.

families.name: Supertrend
families.idea_html:
A vote rather than a signal: three SuperTrend instances with different lengths and multipliers (1_10, 2_11, 3_12) all have to point up for the long and all down for the short, so the strategy trades only when three versions of the same indicator agree. Nothing else is consulted, and the risk is a 0.25 stoploss with a ROI ladder reaching 2,880 minutes.

Caveat: The canonical file of the revision read here is a repaired file (user_data/profile_repairs/Supertrend.py), so the sentence describes the repaired revision; the same family is also present from repositories.

families.name: NASOS
families.idea_html:
Hull moving average(50), EMA(100), SMA(9) and an RSI set on 5m, with the vetoes separated from the conditions: `dont_buy_conditions` is its own list, so the file distinguishes 'do not buy' from 'buy', and `confirm_trade_exit` (29 to 30 lines) is a second exit gate behind the sell signal. families.name: SmoothScalp
families.idea_html:
The base of the ReinforcedSmoothScalp idea, with a smaller profit target: the same EMA(5) high/low band, ADX, MFI, stochastic and CCI columns, and the same one-line entry and exit expressions, but a ROI of 1% and a 50% stoploss instead of 2% and 10%. Because the docstring is identical, the two families are the same author's two settings of one scalp - the 'reinforced' one adds the per-condition switches and halves the risk.

Caveat: Eight of the nine strategies extract to the same 14 indicator calls and the same two conditions; SmoothScalp_476 is the only one that differs (66 lines, nine calls, timeframe written as '1T', ROI 5% and stoploss -0.1). The numbering is a harvest counter, as in the other families of this batch.
version_rows: 76 to 78 lines. The visible differences are colourless: `ta.STOCHF(dataframe, 5.0, 3.0, 0.0, 3.0, 0.0)` against `ta.STOCHF(dataframe, 5, 3, 0, 3, 0)` (float against int arguments), ticker_interval against timeframe, and the stoploss alternating between -0.5 and -0.05.

families.name: Slope
families.idea_html: A pure swing-point reversal: scipy.signal.argrelextrema marks the local minima and maxima of the close over a rolling 64-bar window, a fresh local minimum opens a long and a fresh local maximum closes it, with the short side mirrored. There is no stoploss and no profit target in the usual sense - stoploss -0.999 and minimal_roi 1 mean the trade only ends when the opposite extreme appears.
version_rows: The rule itself never changes: argrelextrema(close, order=5) over a 64-bar window and the mirrored exit are identical in every revision. What moves is the risk block, which is why the family is a good example of a corpus that varies one thing at a time.
V1 trades 30m with no indicator calls, V2 moves to 15m, cuts the stoploss from -0.133 to -0.344 and rebuilds the ROI ladder.

V3 is the largest revision (143 lines) and moves ROI, stoploss and the trailing offset again; V4 removes the protections() block; V5 arms the trailing stop at a 1% offset; V6 adds a minus_di condition and raises the offset to 6.5%.
The revision the description is read from drops the extra indicators and the stop as well: stoploss -0.999 and trailing off, so only the opposite extremum ends a trade.

families.name: AwesomeMacd
families.idea_html: AwesomeMacd: On a 1h timeframe, this strategy enters long when MACD is above zero and the Awesome Oscillator crosses from below zero to above zero. It exits when MACD is below zero and the Awesome Oscillator crosses from above zero to below zero. ADX is calculated but not used in the rules, and it uses a 10% minimal ROI and a -25% stoploss.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On a 1h timeframe, this strategy disables long entries and enters short when MACD is below zero and the Awesome Oscillator crosses from above zero to below zero. It exits the short when MACD is above zero and the Awesome Oscillator crosses from below zero to above zero. It uses a 10% minimal ROI and a -25% stoploss.

On a 1h timeframe, this strategy enters long when MACD is positive and the Awesome Oscillator crosses from below zero to above zero. It exits when MACD is negative and the Awesome Oscillator crosses from above zero to below zero. It uses a 10% minimal ROI and a -25% stoploss.

On a 1h timeframe, this strategy enters long when MACD is above its signal line and the Awesome Oscillator is rising. It exits when MACD is below its signal line and the Awesome Oscillator is falling. It uses a 80% minimal ROI and a -1.6% stoploss.

On a 5m timeframe, this strategy enters long when MACD is positive and the Awesome Oscillator crosses from below zero to above zero. It exits when MACD is negative and the Awesome Oscillator crosses from above zero to below zero. It uses a 10% minimal ROI, a -12% stoploss, and trailing stop enabled.

This strategy enters long when MACD is positive and the Awesome Oscillator crosses from below zero to above zero. The sell signal is set to zero, so exits rely on minimal ROI and stoploss rather than a populated sell signal. It uses a 10% minimal ROI and a -25% stoploss; no timeframe is stated.

families.name: BB_RTR
families.idea_html: BB_RTR: This 5m strategy computes Bollinger Bands, CCI, RMI, Stochastic RSI and pump/crash filters. Entries use dip conditions with RMI/CCI/SRSI oversold and optional break conditions based on Bollinger width/delta; exits are left to ROI, stoploss and custom exit hooks. It has a -1 stoploss and minimal ROI of 0.10.

other_descriptions.idea_html: This 5m strategy computes Bollinger Bands, CCI, RMI and Stochastic RSI plus pump and crash change filters. Entry code defines strict/loose/mid pump protections and crash conditions using tpct_change thresholds, with RSI and EWO checks; exits are all zeros, so trades are closed by ROI, stoploss or custom exit. It uses a -0.333 stoploss and minimal ROI of 0.10.

The fact sheet only shows position adjustment enabled and an adjust_trade_position hook. No timeframe, indicator, entry or exit logic is provided. It is treated as other because the trading logic cannot be determined from this sheet.

The sell trend is disabled in the shown code, and the final buy condition is truncated in the fact sheet.

families.name: ClucHAnix_hhll
families.idea_html: ClucHAnix_hhll: On 5m candles, it buys when the Heikin-Ashi close is below a lower Bollinger band or EMA(50), with 1h ROC and hh/ll differences above thresholds. The dip entry also uses Bollinger-band delta, close delta, and tail conditions. Exits use Fisher/Heikin-Ashi weakness or a momentum-style condition with SMA/EMA and RSI, with stoploss -0.99 and no trailing stop.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On 5m candles, it buys when the Heikin-Ashi close is below a lower Bollinger band or EMA(50), with 1h ROC and hh/ll differences above thresholds. The dip entry also uses Bollinger-band delta, close delta, and tail conditions. Exits use Fisher/Heikin-Ashi weakness or a momentum-style condition with SMA/EMA and RSI, with stoploss -0.99 and no trailing stop.

On 5-minute candles it computes Heikin-Ashi prices and a 40-period Bollinger band, then buys when a 1-hour ROC is above its parameter and either the Heikin-Ashi close is below the shifted lower band with band/close deltas and a small tail, or the close is below the EMA50 while under an extra fraction of the lower band, gated by 48-bar high/low difference filters. It sells when the Fisher transform is above a level with lower Heikin-Ashi highs and closes, EMA3 above the close and close above a fraction of the middle band, or on close above SMA9 and EMA24 times an offset with RSI above 50. It uses a staged ROI table, stoploss -0.99 and no trailing stop.

A 15-minute futures class whose fact sheet shows Heikin-Ashi and 40-period Bollinger band indicators, but the concrete entry and exit rules live in inherited populate_buy_trend/populate_sell_trend methods that are not shown; the entry and exit hooks only delegate to them. Class settings are an ROI table, stoploss -0.99, no trailing stop, startup of 168 candles, plus custom exit, custom stoploss, leverage and informative-pair hooks.

A 15-minute short-capable futures class whose sheet lists Heikin-Ashi and 40-period Bollinger band indicators, while the actual entry and exit logic sits in inherited populate_buy_trend/populate_sell_trend methods that are not shown and are simply called by the entry/exit hooks. Class settings are an ROI table, stoploss -0.99, no trailing stop, 168 startup candles, and custom exit, custom stoploss, leverage and informative-pair hooks.

This class subclasses the ClucHAnix strategy and reuses its buy signal by calling super().populate_buy_trend, then adds trailing-buy order handling: when a buy signal appears with trailing enabled it starts a trailing entry, and while a trailing buy order is active it keeps forcing buy=1 on new candles. Only the confirm_trade_entry hook and the trailing-buy management code are shown; the underlying indicator and exit logic are inherited and not present in the sheet.

families.name: CofiBitStrategy
families.idea_html: CofiBitStrategy: On the 5m timeframe, it buys when open is below the EMA of the low, fast stochastic %K crosses above %D with both below 30, and ADX is above 30. It exits when open is at or above the EMA of the high or when stochastic crosses above 70. Stoploss is -0.25 with tiered minimal ROI.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On the 5m timeframe, it buys when open is below the EMA of the low, fast stochastic %K crosses above %D with both below a buy threshold, and ADX is above a buy threshold. It exits when open is at or above the EMA of the high or when stochastic crosses above a sell threshold. Stoploss is -0.25 with tiered minimal ROI.

On the 15m timeframe, it buys when open is below the EMA of the low, fast stochastic %K crosses above %D with both below 30, and ADX is above 30. It exits when open is at or above the EMA of the high or when stochastic crosses above 70. Stoploss is -0.25 with tiered minimal ROI.

families.name: EMASkipPump
families.idea_html: EMASkipPump: On the 5m timeframe, this strategy buys when the close is below both the short and medium EMAs, equals the medium-term lowest low, is at or below the lower Bollinger band, and volume is below 20x its 30-bar average (pump protection). It sells when the close is above both EMAs, at or above the medium-term high and at or above the upper Bollinger band. It uses a -0.05 stoploss and a minimal ROI of 0.1.

other_descriptions.idea_html: This strategy buys when the close is below both the short and medium EMAs, at the medium-term lowest low, at or below the lower Bollinger band, and volume is below 20x its 30-bar average. It sells when the close is above both EMAs, at or above the medium-term high and at or above the middle Bollinger band. It has a -0.05 stoploss and a stepped minimal-ROI ladder starting at 0.1.

On the 5m timeframe, this strategy enters long when the close is below both the short and medium EMAs, equals the medium-term lowest low, is at or below 0.92 times the lower Bollinger band, and volume is below 20x its 30-bar average. It exits when the close is above both EMAs, at or above the medium-term high and at or above 1.03 times the upper Bollinger band. It carries a -0.05 stoploss and a minimal ROI of 3.

It sells when the close is above both EMAs, at or above the medium-term high and at or above the upper Bollinger band. No timeframe is specified; it uses a -0.05 stoploss and a minimal ROI of 0.1.

It exits when close rises above both EMAs, the EMA-period high, and the upper Bollinger Band. It has a minimal ROI schedule starting at 2.0 and a -0.96 stoploss.

families.name: FastSupertrend_optim
families.idea_html: FastSupertrend_optim3: FastSupertrend_optim3 trades on a 1-hour timeframe, can short, and uses three SuperTrend buy and three SuperTrend sell indicators. It enters long when all buy SuperTrends are 'up' and enters short when all sell SuperTrends are 'down', with volume positive. It exits long when supertrend_3_sell is 'down' and exits short when supertrend_3_buy is 'up'; stoploss is -0.1 with trailing stop.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On the 1h timeframe, it enters long when two buy-side Supertrends are up, RSI EMA is below 75, and volume is positive; it enters short when two sell-side Supertrends are down, RSI EMA is above 25, and volume is positive. It exits long when supertrend_2_sell is down and exits short when supertrend_2_buy is up. It uses a -0.1 stoploss, trailing stop enabled, can short, and has minimal ROI 0.99.

On the 1h timeframe, it enters long when two buy-side Supertrends are up, RSI EMA is below 75, and volume is positive; it enters short when two sell-side Supertrends are down, RSI EMA is above 25, and volume is positive. It exits long when supertrend_2_sell is down and exits short when supertrend_2_buy is up. It uses a -0.025 stoploss, trailing stop enabled, can short, and has minimal ROI 0.99.

On 1h it enters long when two buy-side SuperTrend lines are up and RSI EMA is below 75, and enters short when two sell-side SuperTrend lines are down and RSI EMA is above 25. Exits long or short when the opposite SuperTrend flip occurs. It uses a 5% stoploss, trailing stop, and can_short is enabled.

Exits long or short when the opposite SuperTrend flip occurs. It uses a 5% stoploss, trailing stop, and can_short is enabled.

families.name: HarmonicDivergence
families.idea_html: HarmonicDivergence: On 15m, it enters long when the shifted resampled total_bullish_divergences value is above zero, two_bands_check passes, and volume is above zero. The exit signal is set to zero, so exits rely on custom_exit/custom_stoploss hooks; minimal ROI is 0.007 and stoploss is -2%.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On 15m, it enters long when the shifted resampled total_bullish_divergences value is above zero, two_bands_check passes, and volume is above zero. families.name: JustROCR
families.idea_html: JustROCR: This strategy computes a 499-period Rate of Change Ratio (ROCR) and enters a long trade when ROCR is above 1.10. It has no sell signal in populate_sell_trend, so exits are handled by the minimal ROI of 20%, a 20% stoploss, and trailing stop. The timeframe is not specified in the sheet.

other_descriptions.idea_html: This strategy computes a 499-period ROCR and enters long when ROCR is above 1.20. It has no sell signal in populate_sell_trend, so exits are managed by a 5% minimal ROI, a 1% stoploss, and trailing stop. The timeframe is not specified.

This strategy computes a 499-period ROCR and enters long when ROCR is above 1.10. It has no sell signal in populate_sell_trend, so exits are managed by a 50% minimal ROI, a 1% stoploss, and trailing stop. The timeframe is not specified.

This strategy computes ROCR over periods 499, 200, 100, and 20 and enters long when all four ROCR values exceed their respective thresholds. It has no sell signal in populate_sell_trend, so exits use a 15% minimal ROI, a 15% stoploss, and no trailing stop. The timeframe is not specified.

This strategy computes ROCR over periods 5 and 2 and enters long when both are above 1.10 and 1.01 respectively. It has no sell signal in populate_sell_trend, so exits use a 5% minimal ROI, a 1% stoploss, and trailing stop. The timeframe is not specified.

families.name: MultiRSI
families.idea_html: MultiRSI: On a 5m timeframe, it calculates SMA5, SMA200, and resampled RSIs on 2x and 8x intervals. It enters when SMA5 is at or above SMA200 and the base RSI is more than 20 points below the 8x resampled RSI. It exits when the base RSI is above both the 2x and 8x resampled RSIs. Stoploss is -0.05 and minimal ROI is 0.01.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On a 5m timeframe, it resamples RSI on 2x and 12x intervals. It buys when the 12x resampled RSI is rising and the base RSI crosses above 35 from at or below 35. There is no sell signal, so exits come from ROI or the trailing stop; stoploss is -0.20.

families.name: NOTankAi
families.idea_html: NOTankAi15: On 15m, it enters long when RSI is below the buy threshold while EMA50 is above EMA200, and enters short when RSI is above the sell threshold while EMA50 is below EMA200. Long exits when RSI exceeds the sell threshold, and short exits when RSI falls below the buy threshold. It uses stoploss -0.10, trailing stop true, and a minimal ROI ladder.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On 15m, it enters long at a local price minimum when RSI is below 30, DI_catch is active, no recent maxima are present, a prior minima exists, and volume is positive. It exits long at a local maximum or when maxima_check/volume conditions trigger, with position adjustment enabled. Stoploss is -0.99 and minimal ROI starts at 50%.

On 15m, it enters long at a local price minimum when RSI is below 30, DI_catch is active, no recent maxima are present, a prior minima exists, and volume is positive. It exits long at a local maximum or when maxima_check/volume conditions trigger, with position adjustment enabled. Stoploss is -0.99 and minimal ROI starts at 50%.

On 15m, it can trade long and short, using adjustable RSI thresholds around 30 for long entries and 70 for short entries, combined with DI_catch, local extrema, maxima/minima checks, and optional continuous, trend, and volume filters. Exits are RSI-threshold based and also use local maxima/minima conditions. It has stoploss -0.99, position adjustment enabled, and can_short=True.

This 15m strategy computes RSI, DI difference, local maxima/minima, and Murrey math levels. Entries are gated by DI_catch, maxima_check, and RSI thresholds (long below about 30, short above about 70), aiming to buy minima and sell maxima. Exits use opposite RSI thresholds with extrema signals; position adjustment is enabled up to two times and the stoploss is -0.99.

This 15m strategy uses RSI, DI difference, and local minima/maxima. It enters long at prior minima when RSI is below 30 and DI_catch is active, with variants such as Minima Full Send. Exits occur on maxima_check or maxima extrema signals; position adjustment is enabled up to two times and stoploss is -0.99.

families.name: QuickAdapter
families.idea_html: QuickAdapterV3: This strategy uses FreqAI model outputs. It enters long when the model predicts do_predict==1, the DI catch filter is 1, and the predicted extrema is below the minima sort threshold; symmetric short conditions exist but can_short is false. The exit signal code returns the dataframe unchanged, so trades are closed by custom_exit, ROI, or the -4% stoploss.

other_descriptions.idea_html: This strategy uses FreqAI model outputs. It enters long when do_predict==1, the DI catch is 1, and the predicted extrema is below the minima sort threshold, and enters short when the predicted extrema is above the maxima sort threshold. Exit signals are not populated, so exits rely on custom_exit, ROI, or the -4% stoploss; shorting is enabled.

It enters long when do_predict==1, DI catch is 1, and predicted extrema is below the minima sort threshold, with symmetric short entries above the maxima threshold. Exit signals are not populated, and trailing stop is enabled along with a -4% stoploss and custom_exit hook.

This strategy uses FreqAI model outputs with additional return thresholds. It enters long when do_predict==1, DI catch is 1, predicted extrema is below the minima sort threshold, and predicted max return is at least 1.5%; short entries require predicted min return magnitude at least 1.5% and extrema above the maxima threshold. Exit signals are not populated, and trailing stop plus a -4% stoploss are configured.

It is a can-short strategy.

families.idea_html: Quickie: Buys when ADX >30, TEMA is below the Bollinger middle band but rising, and close is below SMA200. Sells when ADX >70, TEMA is above the middle band and falling. Timeframe 5m with a -25% stoploss and ROI schedule.

families.name: SMAOffset
families.idea_html: SMAOffset: On the 5m timeframe, the strategy buys when close is below a moving-average buy offset and volume is positive. It sells when close is above a moving-average sell offset with positive volume, using a -0.5 stoploss, minimal ROI, and a custom_stoploss hook without trailing stop.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On 5m candles, it enters long when close crosses above an MA offset (moving average times low_offset) and exits when close crosses below an MA offset (moving average times high_offset). It uses a -0.5 stoploss, minimal ROI tiers, a trailing stop, and a custom_stoploss hook.

families.name: el_extrema
families.idea_html: Dip-buying at detected extrema with an EWO momentum filter: a local minimum of the close (argrelextrema, order 5) plus price below EMA(entry length) times low_offset, and then either an EWO above the high threshold with RSI below the entry level or an EWO below the low threshold, opens the long; the short side is the mirror at local maxima. Exits are the ROI ladder (50% at entry decaying to 2% after five days) plus a 5% stoploss. The offsets, EMA lengths, RSI level and both EWO thresholds are hyperopt parameters, so the revision in the corpus is one point in a search space.

families.idea_html: CustomStrategy: On 1h candles, it defines a sideways market when the 12-bar price amplitude is small, Bollinger band width is <= 0.1, and RSI is neutral. It buys in that sideways market when MACD is above zero and the candle's upper and lower wicks are each at most 40% of candle length. Exits are triggered by two consecutive doji candles or, when in a sideways market, by a close below the recorded sideways start.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On 1h timeframe, it detects 12-candle sideways markets where the price range is at most 8% and marks the range low. It buys when the close is at or below that sideways low. It exits when a subsequent close is below the sideways low; stoploss is -10% and minimal_roi is disabled.

On 1h timeframe, it identifies sideways markets using a <=8% price range, Bollinger-band width <=0.1, and neutral RSI. It buys when that sideways condition is active and MACD is above zero. It exits when price closes below the sideways low; stoploss is -10% and minimal_roi is disabled.

On 1h timeframe, it detects sideways markets with <=8% range, Bollinger-band width <=0.1, and neutral RSI, then buys when MACD is above zero. It exits when two consecutive doji candles appear or when price closes below the sideways low. Stoploss is -10% and minimal_roi is disabled.

families.name: DoubleEMACrossoverWithTrend
families.idea_html: DoubleEMACrossoverWithTrend: DoubleEMACrossoverWithTrend enters on a 1h candle when EMA9 crosses above EMA21 and the candle low is above EMA200. It exits when EMA9 crosses below EMA21 or the candle low falls below EMA200. Stoploss is -0.2 and trailing stop is disabled.

other_descriptions.idea_html: DoubleEMACrossoverWithTrend_158 enters on a 1h candle when EMA9 crosses above EMA21 and the candle low is above EMA200. It exits when EMA9 crosses below EMA21 or the candle low falls below EMA200. Stoploss is -0.2 and trailing stop is disabled.

DoubleEMACrossoverWithTrend_197 enters on a 1h candle when EMA9 crosses above EMA21 and the candle low is above EMA200. It exits when EMA9 crosses below EMA21 or the candle low falls below EMA200. Stoploss is -0.2, trailing stop is disabled, and a minimal ROI schedule is configured.

DoubleEMACrossoverWithTrend_37 enters on a 1h candle when EMA9 crosses above EMA21 and the candle low is above EMA200. It exits when EMA9 crosses below EMA21 or the candle low falls below EMA200. Stoploss is -0.2 and trailing stop is disabled.

families.name: EVA
families.idea_html: EVA1: On 15m, it enters long when slow RSI is falling, fast RSI is below a threshold, RSI is above another threshold, close is below SMA 15 by a parameter offset, and CTI is below a threshold. It uses a custom_exit hook and no exit signal code, with minimal ROI set to 1 and a -0.25 stoploss.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On 1h, it enters long when slow RSI is falling, fast RSI is below a threshold, RSI is above another threshold, close is below SMA 15 by a parameter offset, and CTI is below a threshold. It uses a custom_exit hook and no exit signal code, with minimal ROI set to 1 and a -0.25 stoploss.
On 15m, it enters long when fast RSI is above 50, RSI is above 50, and CTI is below 0. It uses a custom_exit hook and no exit signal code, with minimal ROI set to 1 and a -0.25 stoploss.

On 15m, it enters long when an SMA-aligned uptrend condition switches off and close is below SMA 5 by a parameter percentage. It uses a custom_exit hook and no exit signal code, with minimal ROI set to 1 and a -0.25 stoploss.

families.name: EnsembleStrategy
families.idea_html: EnsembleStrategy: It delegates buy signals to a combination of strategies selected at runtime by buy_strategies. It enters when the mean of those strategy buy signals exceeds buy_action_diff_threshold. The sell signal is set to 0, and it has a custom_stoploss hook, stoploss -0.99, and minimal ROI 100.0; no timeframe is shown.

other_descriptions.idea_html: It delegates buy and sell signals to runtime-selected strategy combinations. It enters when the mean buy signal exceeds buy_mean_threshold and exits when the mean sell signal exceeds sell_mean_threshold. It uses a trailing stop and -0.203 stoploss, with minimal ROI steps; no timeframe is shown.

It delegates buy signals to runtime-selected strategies with exceptions ignored. It enters when the mean buy signal, after fillna(0), exceeds buy_mean_threshold. The sell signal is set to 0, and it uses a custom_sell hook, trailing stop, and -0.148 stoploss; no timeframe is shown.

EnsembleStrategy_2 runs each base strategy to generate indicator columns and buy/sell signal columns, then builds CatBoost classifier datasets from the populated dataframe. It sets the buy signal when the predicted buy probability is above 0.7, and it similarly computes sell signals through a model-based process. The fact sheet does not show a timeframe, stoploss, or ROI setting.

families.name: FileLoadingStrategy
families.idea_html: FileLoadingStrategy: It has no indicator population logic; entries are driven by an external strategy_data record for the pair. When the stored status is PENDING, it sets the entry signal, marks status HOLDING, and records the close price as entry_price. The exit method is empty and stoploss is -1.0.

other_descriptions.idea_html: It has no market indicators; populate_entry_trend reads strategy data from the order handler and sets an entry signal only when the pair status is PENDING, then updates it to HOLDING. If the pair is not pending, it sets no entry. There is no exit logic and stoploss is -1.0.

The strategy computes no indicators at all; populate_indicators just returns the dataframe. Entries are driven by external state: if the order handler reports a PENDING status for the pair, an entry signal is set and the stored status is moved to HOLDING, otherwise no entry is set. The exit method is empty and the stoploss is -1.0.

No indicators are calculated. An entry is triggered only when the order handler holds a PENDING record for the pair; the strategy then sets the entry signal, records the last close as entry_price and switches the status to HOLDING. The exit method is empty and the stoploss is -1.0.

families.name: GuruSkippyasurmuni
families.idea_html: GuruSkippyasurmuni: The strategy calls condition_generator three times with hyperoptable indicator, crossed-indicator, operator, and real-number parameters for entry and sell signals, while populate_indicators only initializes custom_info. It runs on 5m with minimal_roi set to 1000.0, stoploss -0.35, trailing_stop False, and position adjustment enabled with max_entry_position_adjustment 4.

other_descriptions.idea_html: The strategy uses condition_generator with hyperoptable indicator/operator parameters for buy and sell conditions, and populate_indicators only initializes custom_info. It runs on 5m with minimal_roi set to 1000.0, stoploss -1.0, trailing_stop False, and position adjustment enabled with max_entry_position_adjustment 24.

The strategy uses condition_generator with hyperoptable indicator/operator parameters for buy and sell conditions, and populate_indicators only initializes custom_info. families.name: HLHB
families.idea_html: HLHB: 4h strategy. It enters long when RSI crosses above 50, EMA5 crosses above EMA10, ADX is above 25, and volume is positive. It exits when RSI crosses below 50 and EMA5 crosses below EMA10 with ADX above 25, using minimal ROI and a trailing stop.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On the 4h timeframe it enters long when RSI(10) crosses above 50, EMA5 crosses above EMA10 and ADX is above 25 with non-zero volume. It exits long on the mirrored crosses below 50 and below EMA10 while ADX stays above 25. A trailing stop, the minimal ROI table and a -0.3211 stoploss manage the position.

On the 4h timeframe, it enters long when RSI crosses above 50, EMA5 crosses above EMA10, ADX is above 25, and volume is non-zero. It exits on the inverse RSI and EMA crosses with ADX still above 25. It uses a trailing stop, a stoploss of -0.3211, and a stepped minimal ROI.

On the 15m timeframe, it enters long when RSI crosses above 50, EMA5 crosses above EMA10, ADX is above 25, and volume is non-zero. It exits on the inverse RSI and EMA crosses with ADX still above 25. It uses a trailing stop, a stoploss of -0.3211, and a stepped minimal ROI.

families.name: HPStrategy
families.idea_html: HPStrategy: 1m strategy. It enters long on dip-buying conditions: price below an EMA14 factor with low RSI, or below a moving average with low RSI and EWO oscillator conditions. It uses position adjustment and custom sell logic, with exits on strength above HMA50/moving averages and RSI above 50, plus ROI and trailing stop.

other_descriptions.idea_html: 15m strategy. It enters long when CCI is below -100 and RSI is below 30 with positive volume. It exits when CCI is above 100 and RSI is above 70 with positive volume, using position adjustment, ROI, and trailing stop.

1m strategy. It enters long on dip-buying conditions: price below an EMA14 factor with low RSI, or below moving averages with low RSI and EWO oscillator conditions. It exits on strength above HMA50/moving averages and RSI above 50, using position adjustment, ROI, and trailing stop.

1m strategy. It enters long on dip-buying conditions: price below an EMA14 factor with low RSI, or below moving averages with low RSI and EWO oscillator conditions. It exits on strength above HMA50/moving averages and RSI above 50, using position adjustment, ROI, and trailing stop.

families.name: Hacklemore
families.idea_html: Hacklemore: On 5m, it enters long when the informative-timeframe EMA3 is above EMA12, the informative MACD is above its signal, up_trend is 1, RMI-slow is at least 55 and rising, MACD histogram is positive, SAR is below close, and recent closes are higher, with volume above zero and below a 30x volume mean cap. Exits use sell signals based on a dn_trend, RMI-fast below 50, current profit negative but above stoploss, and average other-trade profit; ROI and stoploss are set (-8.5%).

other_descriptions.idea_html: On 15m, it enters long when up_trend is true, RMI is above 55 and above its 3-period mean, recent closes are higher, SAR is below close for three bars, and volume is below a 30x volume mean cap. Exit signals use dn_trend with RMI below 30 and current profit above -3%; ROI schedule and trailing stop with a -99% stoploss are configured.

On 5m, it enters long when up_trend is 1, RMI is above 55 and above its 3-period mean, closes are rising, SAR is below close, and volume is below a 30x volume mean cap. Exit signals for an open trade use dn_trend, RMI below 50, and positive volume when current profit is negative; ROI and a -99% stoploss with trailing stop are set.
This 1h strategy defines ROI and stoploss attributes but the indicator, entry, and exit code sections are empty. No trading logic can be derived from the fact sheet.

families.name: KamaFama
families.idea_html: KamaFama_2025: This 5m strategy computes MAMA, FAMA, KAMA, Williams %R, CTI, RSI, and stochastic indicators. It enters long when KAMA is above FAMA and FAMA is above a fraction of MAMA, while Williams %R, CTI, and mama_diff are weak, RSI(84/112) is below 60, and price is below recent 48-bar and 288-bar highs. There is no exit signal in populate_exit_trend; exits are handled by custom_exit and custom_stoploss hooks, a 100% minimal ROI, and a 33% stoploss.

other_descriptions.idea_html: This 5m strategy uses the same entry logic as KamaFama_2025: it enters long when KAMA > FAMA, FAMA > MAMA * 0.981, Williams %R < -61.3, mama_diff < -0.025, CTI < -0.715, price is at least 5% below the 48-bar high and 12.5% below the 288-bar high, and RSI(84/112) < 60. There is no exit signal in populate_exit_trend; exits are handled by custom_exit and custom_stoploss hooks, a 100% minimal ROI, and a 25% stoploss. It also has a leverage hook and uses 400 startup candles.

This 5m strategy computes MAMA, FAMA, KAMA, Williams %R, CTI, RSI, and stochastic indicators. It enters long when MAMA > KAMA > FAMA, mama_diff > 0.02, CTI > 0.7, Williams %R > -61.3, RSI(84/112) < 60, and the current candle is bullish (open < close). There is no exit signal in populate_exit_trend; exits are handled by custom_exit and custom_stoploss hooks, a 100% minimal ROI, and a 25% stoploss.

This 5m strategy uses the same trend-following entry as KamaFama_3_1: MAMA > KAMA > FAMA, mama_diff > 0.02, CTI > 0.7, Williams %R > -61.3, RSI(84/112) < 60, and a bullish candle. There is no exit signal in populate_exit_trend; exits are handled by a custom_stoploss hook and a minimal ROI schedule of 10% at 0m, 5% at 60m, 3% at 120m, and 1% at 180m. The stoploss is 25%.

families.name: Low_BB
families.idea_html: Low_BB: On a 1m timeframe, it buys when close is at or below 0.98 times the lower Bollinger band, using Bollinger bands on typical price and close plus MACD indicators. The exit code sets the sell column with an empty condition, and risk is managed by a tiered minimal ROI and a -0.015 stoploss.

other_descriptions.idea_html: It buys when close is at or below 0.98 times the lower Bollinger band, using Bollinger bands on typical price and close plus MACD indicators. The exit code contains an empty sell condition, and risk is managed by a tiered minimal ROI and a -0.015 stoploss; no timeframe is specified.

On a 1m timeframe, it buys when close is at or below 0.98 times the lower Bollinger band, with Bollinger bands and MACD populated. The exit code sets sell to 0 with an empty condition, and risk is managed by a tiered minimal ROI and a -0.015 stoploss.

It enters long when the close is at or below 98% of the lower Bollinger band, which is calculated from typical price with a 20-period window and 2 standard deviations. The exit code sets no sell signals, so positions are closed by the minimal ROI or the -1.5% stoploss. The timeframe is not specified.

families.name: NFI
families.idea_html: NFI46: On 5m candles, it buys dips when the 1h EMA50 is above EMA200 and 1h/5m RSI and MFI are low, with safe_dips and safe_pump filters and price near the lower Bollinger band. It exits when RSI is high and price has closed above the upper Bollinger band for several candles. Stoploss is -0.99, minimal ROI is 10 at 0 minutes, and custom sell logic is present.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On a 5m timeframe with 1h informative indicators, entry requires a 1h EMA50 above EMA200 and a rising SMA200, together with dip conditions such as RSI and MFI below thresholds or close under a lower Bollinger band offset. Exit signals fire when RSI is high and close has been above the upper Bollinger band for six consecutive candles. Stoploss is -0.99 and minimal ROI is 10 (1000%).

On a 5m timeframe with 1h informative indicators, entry requires a 1h EMA50 above EMA200 and a rising SMA200, together with dip conditions such as RSI and MFI below thresholds or close under a lower Bollinger band offset. Exit signals fire when RSI is high and close has been above the bb20_2_upp band for six consecutive candles. Stoploss is -0.99 and minimal ROI is 10 (1000%).

It buys when RSI crosses below a bull or bear threshold, depending on the higher-timeframe regime, and sells when RSI exceeds the corresponding sell threshold. It has a -0.30 stoploss, custom stoploss, and a tiered ROI.

families.name: QuickBuyStrategy
families.idea_html: QuickBuyStrategy: Buys when close is above the Bollinger midband. Sells when RSI crosses above 70 while close is above the midband. Timeframe 1h with a -10% stoploss and a ROI schedule.

other_descriptions.idea_html: Buys when close is above the Bollinger midband. Sells when RSI crosses above 70 while close is above the midband. Timeframe 1hr with a -10% stoploss and a ROI schedule.

On the 1-hour timeframe it enters long whenever the close is above the Bollinger midband, with no other entry condition. It exits when RSI crosses above 70 while price is still above the midband. Risk control is a minimal ROI ladder (4% at 0 minutes, 0% at 40) and a -10% stoploss, no trailing stop.

Remaining shown code is trade-manager state and desktop notifications. There is a -0.99 stoploss and a 10 minimal ROI with no trailing stop.

families.name: Ralli
families.idea_html: RalliV1: On 5-minute candles, it buys when the selected buy EMA is below EMA100, SMA9 is below that buy EMA, fast RSI is between 4 and 35, price is below the buy EMA by a low offset, EWO is above a high threshold, RSI is below a buy threshold, and volume is positive. It sells when HMA50 is above EMA100 and price is above SMA9 and above a sell EMA by a high offset with fast RSI above slow RSI, or when price is below EMA100 but above a sell EMA high offset with fast RSI above slow RSI. It uses minimal ROI tiers from 0.04 down to 0, a -0.3 stoploss, no trailing stop, and a custom stoploss hook.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On 5-minute candles, it uses the same dip-buy conditions as RalliV1: selected buy EMA below EMA100, SMA9 below that EMA, fast RSI between 4 and 35, price below the buy EMA by an offset, EWO above a threshold, RSI below a buy threshold, and volume positive. Its populate_sell_trend sets the sell column to 0, so exits are handled by minimal ROI tiers and the -0.3 stoploss rather than a sell signal. It has custom_sell and custom_stoploss hooks and no trailing stop.

families.name: SMAOG
families.idea_html: SMAOG: On the 5m timeframe, the strategy buys when EMA50 is above EMA200, close is above EMA200, the pair is not marked bad by rolling drawdown checks, and close is below a buy MA offset. It exits when close is above a sell MA offset and the open or 2-period RSI is weakening, using a -0.23 stoploss, trailing stop, and minimal ROI.

families.name: SMAOffset_Hippocritical
families.idea_html: SMAOffset_Hippocritical_dca: On 5m candles, it enters long when close is below an EMA times low_offset and either EWO is above ewo_high with RSI below a buy threshold, or EWO is below ewo_low, while missing-data count is low. families.name: SmaRsiStrategy
families.idea_html: SmaRsiStrategy: On the daily timeframe, it uses RSI and a 21-period SMA. It buys when RSI is above 50 and close crosses above the 21 SMA. It sells when RSI is below 50 and close crosses below the 21 SMA, with a -10% stoploss and a minimal ROI of 99%.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On the daily timeframe, it computes RSI and 21/50-period SMAs, but entry and exit only use RSI and the 21 SMA. It buys when RSI is above 50 and close crosses above the 21 SMA, and sells when RSI is below 50 and close crosses below the 21 SMA. It uses a -10% stoploss and a minimal ROI of 99%.

families.name: Strategy001_custom_sell
families.idea_html: Strategy001_custom_sell: On 5m timeframe, computes EMA20, EMA50, EMA100, Heikin-Ashi values and RSI. It enters when EMA20 crosses above EMA50, the Heikin-Ashi close is above EMA20, and the Heikin-Ashi bar is green. It exits when EMA50 crosses above EMA100, the Heikin-Ashi close is below EMA20, and the Heikin-Ashi bar is red. Stoploss is -10% and minimal ROI is defined.

families.name: TaSearch30m

families.name: Tesla
families.idea_html: Tesla4_2: On 5m with 15m informative data, it enters when vol_base is below -80, fast RSI is below a threshold, close is below a moving-average offset, EWO is above a threshold, RSI is below a threshold, and close is below a sell moving-average offset. It also has a don't-buy pump protection based on the 15m rolling maximum close compared with the current close. Exits use combinations of SMA/HMA and RSI conditions, with trailing stop and ROI.

other_descriptions.idea_html: On 5m candles with a 15m informative timeframe, it enters long when RSI fast and RSI are below thresholds, price is below a buy moving average by an offset, and EWO is above a threshold; a second variant adds RSI below 25 and a different low offset. It exits when price is above SMA_9 and a sell moving average with RSI above 50 and fast RSI above slow RSI, or in a weaker-price condition with HMA_50. It uses a -0.15 stoploss, custom sell/stoploss hooks, and a dont-buy condition based on a 15m rolling maximum.

A 5m strategy that buys when close is below a moving average multiplied by a low offset, fast RSI and RSI are low, EWO is above a threshold, and volume exists, with a 15m pump-protection filter. It exits on either close above SMA9 and a high-offset sell moving average with RSI above 50 and fast RSI above slow RSI, or close below HMA50 with close above a sell moving average and fast RSI above slow RSI. It uses a 15% stoploss and trailing stop.

A 5m strategy that buys when vol_base is within negative ranges, fast RSI is below 35, close is below a moving average multiplied by a low offset, EWO is above a threshold, RSI is below a buy threshold, and volume exists. It exits on either close above SMA9 and a high-offset sell moving average with RSI above 50 and fast RSI above slow RSI, or close below HMA50 with close above a sell moving average and fast RSI above slow RSI. It uses a 15% stoploss and trailing stop.

It exits when MACD falls below its signal line, EMA5 falls below EMA50, and RSI drops below 40. It uses a -25% stoploss, trailing stop, and minimal ROI targets.

families.name: Vail
families.idea_html: Vail2: Vail2 is a 5-minute strategy that enters long when fast RSI is below 35, the 1-hour trend is positive, and the candle closes below a lower moving average while opening above it. It exits when RSI is high and the close has been above the upper Bollinger band for several candles. It uses a trailing stop, 10% minimal ROI, and a custom exit hook.

It exits when price is above a sell EMA and RSI is high, or when price is below HMA 50 with fast RSI above slow RSI. It uses a trailing stop, 10% minimal ROI, and -30% stoploss.

It has no sell signal, so exits rely on minimal ROI and a trailing stop with stoploss -0.04. It uses 1h informative indicators and a 200-candle startup.

Exit signals are not used, so trades end via the ROI table, the -7% stoploss or the trailing stop.

Sell signals are disabled, ROI is effectively off, and a custom stoploss manages exits.
